raw_response:
I been farming for twenty years now. Never went to school, can't read or write, but I know this land like the back of my hand. I rent all 380 mu here in Huaiqiao, Wangzhaozhuang village — not a single mu is my own. My family got four people, but with this much land we can't work it by ourselves. I got three machines: a tractor, a seeder, and a sprayer. For the big jobs I still need to hire workers.

This year I'm doing the same as last year. Three hundred thirty mu cotton, fifty mu spring maize. Cotton is where the money is. Last year my 802 variety gave me 550 kilos per mu, and I sold it for about 2.88 yuan per kilo. Good enough to pay the rent and have something left for the family. I buy new seed every year — three jin per mu, costs forty-five yuan. Saved seed don't sprout as good, and with 330 mu I can't afford a bad stand.

For cotton, I till with the rotary machine in April — forty yuan per mu, but worth it for a clean seedbed. Then I lay plastic film, four jin per mu. Keeps the soil warm and holds the moisture. I plant around April 14th, harvest around October 24th. For fertilizer, I put down a hundred kilos of that three-fifteen compound per mu before planting, using the machine. That's two bags. When the cotton is growing good, I topdress once with thirty kilos of the high-nitrogen compound — the twenty-eight-six-six one. I broadcast it by hand. Total two times fertilizing.

Cotton is picky about bugs. I spray insecticide twelve times through the season, herbicide three times, and plant regulator four times. Without the regulator the cotton grows tall and thin like a weed, and the bolls don't set right. I irrigate once from the river, border flood, costs ten yuan per mu. Water is getting expensive, so once is enough for cotton if the rain helps some.

The fifty mu of maize I plant May 2nd, harvest September 2nd. Long218 variety, hybrid seed, one package per mu at forty-five yuan. Same tillage and film as cotton. Base fertilizer is eighty kilos of twenty-eight-six-six compound, then I topdress with twenty-five kilos of urea. Irrigate twice. Two sprays for bugs, one for weeds. Harvest with the combine, sixty yuan per mu. Maize gives about 1,500 kilos per mu. The price is lower than cotton — only about ninety fen per kilo — but it's steady money and doesn't need as much fuss.

My family does the supervising, spreading fertilizer by hand, and some spraying. But I hire people for irrigation and cotton picking. With 330 mu of cotton, I need plenty of hands at harvest time — family alone can't do it. I don't count every coin, but I know roughly that seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, film, water, machine work, and wages add up to about 190,000 yuan for the year. That's a lot of money going out. But cotton pays better than grain, and with 380 mu I can spread the risk. If the weather holds and the bollworms don't come heavy, I should clear a profit after paying the rent.

I'm not trying anything new this year. Twenty years taught me that change is risky. My neighbor tried a new cotton variety last year and the yield was poor. I'll stick with 802, same fertilizer, same spray schedule. Good enough is good enough.
